quests.instruction: Dina loves waking at 5:30 to watch the sunrise, so her family calls her an early bird. Her cousin stays up late reading under the covers. She’s a…
quests.hint: Which bird is awake when the moon is out?
quests.explanation: An early bird is someone who loves the start of the day. A night owl comes alive late in the evening.
quests.funFact: Many owls are nocturnal, meaning they are most active at night.

quests.instruction: When Kavya played her favorite game, the hour flew by. During a dull lecture, the same hour…
quests.hint: A boring hour feels very different from a fun one.
quests.explanation: Time that flies by feels very quick. Time that drags feels as though it will never end.
quests.funFact: The saying “time flies when you’re having fun” describes how an enjoyable hour can feel short.

quests.instruction: Which sentence tells the same story in the opposite order as: “Rahul did his homework before dinner.”?
quests.correctAnswer: Rahul did his homework after dinner.
options: Rahul did his homework during dinner.
Rahul did his homework without dinner.
Rahul did his homework after dinner.
quests.hint: Which word swaps the order of homework and dinner?
quests.explanation: Switching “before” to “after” puts the events the other way round. “During” and “without” change the story in different ways.
quests.funFact: The word “before” is built from “be” and “fore”, an old word meaning “in front”.

quests.instruction: Many parts of India get most of their rain during the monsoon, the rainy season. The long months with hardly any rain are the…
quests.hint: What do farmers wait for when the fields are cracking?
quests.explanation: The rainy season brings most of the year’s rainfall. The dry season has very little.
quests.funFact: “Monsoon” comes from an Arabic word meaning “season”.

quests.instruction: At high tide, the sea covers the sandy beach. Several hours later, the water pulls far back at…
quests.hint: Shells are easiest to find when the water has pulled far back.
quests.explanation: High tide is when the sea reaches its highest level on the shore. Low tide is when it falls back.
quests.funFact: Tides are caused mainly by the Moon’s pull on the oceans.

quests.instruction: Mira always forgets her water bottle. Which sentence means the opposite?
quests.correctAnswer: Mira never forgets her water bottle.
options: Mira sometimes forgets her water bottle.
Mira often forgets her water bottle.
Mira never forgets her water bottle.
quests.hint: Opposite means zero times, not just fewer times.
quests.explanation: The opposite of “every time” is “not once”, so “never” is the only match. “Sometimes” and “often” still mean she forgets it now and then.
quests.funFact: Drinking water helps your body stay cool and work well.

quests.instruction: Ana read ten books, Ben read six and Cleo read two. Ana read the most. Cleo read the…
quests.hint: Whose pile of finished books is the smallest?
quests.explanation: Most means the biggest amount. Least means the smallest amount.
quests.funFact: The Library of Congress in the United States is one of the largest libraries in the world.

quests.instruction: Three siblings: Ria is 14, Tej is 11 and little Neha is 6. Ria is the oldest, and Neha is the…
quests.hint: The child with the fewest birthdays has a special name.
quests.explanation: The oldest person has lived the most years. The youngest has lived the fewest.
quests.funFact: Some bristlecone pine trees in California are almost five thousand years old.

quests.instruction: Which sentence says the opposite of: “At 8 a.m., the bus was completely full.”?
quests.correctAnswer: At 11 a.m., the bus was completely empty.
options: At 11 a.m., the bus was completely empty.
At 11 a.m., the bus was completely new.
At 8 a.m., the bus was completely late.
quests.hint: What would you see on board after the rush ends?
quests.explanation: “Full” flips to “empty”, and the quieter time of day makes the picture match. The other choices don’t reverse the idea of crowds.
quests.funFact: “Bus” is short for “omnibus”, a Latin word meaning “for all”.

quests.instruction: Dev scored 10 out of 10 on his spelling test, the best score in the class. Sara scored 2 out of 10, so hers was the…
quests.hint: Which word describes the lowest result of everyone?
quests.explanation: Best means better than all the others. Worst means worse than all the others.
quests.funFact: English spelling is tricky because the language has borrowed words from many other languages.

quests.instruction: Saving two rupees today for a sweet is a short-term goal. Saving a little every month for a whole year to buy a bicycle is a…
quests.hint: Saving for a whole year takes months of patience.
quests.explanation: A short-term goal is reached soon. A long-term goal takes a lot of time.
quests.funFact: A mango tree can take several years before it bears its first fruit.

quests.instruction: Which pair of words are NOT opposites?
quests.hint: Opposites have meanings that are far apart, not close together.
quests.explanation: Big and large mean almost the same thing. Hot–cold and up–down each pull in opposite directions.
quests.funFact: Words with similar meanings are called synonyms, and words with opposite meanings are called antonyms.

quests.instruction: The train was due at 4:00 and arrived at 4:00, so it was on time. Another train, stuck behind a broken signal, was…
quests.hint: What happens to a schedule when a train can’t move?
quests.explanation: On time means arriving exactly as planned. Delayed means arriving later than planned.
quests.funFact: In the 1800s, railways helped push towns across Britain to use one standard time.

quests.instruction: At school, the teacher says, “Start up your computers.” At the end of the lesson, she says, “Please…”
quests.hint: Before leaving the lab, one more thing happens to the computer.
quests.explanation: Starting up switches a computer on and gets it ready. Shutting down switches it off properly.
quests.funFact: The first computers were as big as a whole room.

quests.instruction: Tea A is hotter than tea B. So tea B is…
quests.hint: If one cup is higher on the heat scale, where is the other?
quests.explanation: Hotter and colder are comparisons that work like a seesaw. If A is more hot, then B is less hot, so colder.
quests.funFact: A cup of tea cools faster in a wide cup than in a tall, narrow one because more of the surface touches the air.

quests.instruction: The film was so exciting that Jay stayed awake until the very end. Grandpa, tired after a busy day, began to…
quests.hint: What happens to your eyes when they get heavy?
quests.explanation: Staying awake means keeping alert. Dozing off means slipping into a light sleep.
quests.funFact: Giraffes sleep only a few hours a day.

quests.instruction: A soap bubble bursts in seconds, so it is short-lived. A mountain stays standing for millions of years, so it is…
quests.hint: Think of something that lasts a very long time, like a mountain.
quests.explanation: Short-lived things disappear quickly. Long-lasting things stay for a long time.
quests.funFact: Mountains like the Himalayas are still slowly rising.

quests.instruction: The bakery sign says OPEN in the morning. When the baker finishes work, she flips it to say…
quests.hint: What does the sign tell customers when the shop is shut?
quests.explanation: An “open” sign tells people they can come in. Flipping it to “closed” tells them the shop isn’t serving anymore.
quests.funFact: Bakers often start work before dawn so the bread is fresh in the morning.

quests.instruction: It’s a sunny Saturday, so Zoya’s family decides to go out for a picnic. If it poured all day, they would…
quests.hint: What do people do with a rainy weekend?
quests.explanation: Going out means leaving home for an activity. Staying in means remaining at home.
quests.funFact: Board games have been played for thousands of years. One of the oldest known is Senet, from ancient Egypt.

quests.instruction: Mum says, “Put the toys away now.” If she meant after dinner, she would say, “Put them away…”
quests.hint: Mum doesn’t mean this very minute.
quests.explanation: Now means at this moment. Later means at some time after.
quests.funFact: “Later” is the comparative form of “late”.

quests.instruction: The lift goes up to the tenth floor. Which sentence describes the opposite journey?
quests.correctAnswer: The lift goes down to the ground floor.
options: The lift goes down to the ground floor.
The lift goes slowly to the tenth floor.
The lift goes up to the roof.
quests.hint: Which trip would take you back to the street?
quests.explanation: The opposite of going up is going down, and the ground floor is the opposite end of the building.
quests.funFact: The first safe passenger elevator was demonstrated by Elisha Otis in 1854.

quests.instruction: Pizza cheese is thickest in the middle. The crust sits at the…
quests.hint: Where does the circle end?
quests.explanation: The middle is the center point of something. The edge is where it stops.
quests.funFact: Pizza as we know it began in Naples, Italy.

quests.instruction: Mumbai is urban, with tall buildings and heavy traffic. A small village surrounded by paddy fields is…
quests.hint: Think of a place with farms and fields instead of skyscrapers.
quests.explanation: Urban places are towns and cities. Rural places are in the countryside.
quests.funFact: More than half of the world’s people now live in cities.

quests.instruction: A town on the beach, with fishing boats along the shore, is coastal. A town far from the sea, up in the hills, is…
quests.hint: Which town would you need a long bus ride to reach the sea from?
quests.explanation: Coastal means next to the sea. Inland means away from it.
quests.funFact: Some countries, like Nepal and Bhutan, are landlocked and have no coastline at all.

quests.instruction: Dad jogs every morning before work. Which sentence flips both parts?
quests.correctAnswer: Dad jogs every evening after work.
options: Dad jogs every evening before work.
Dad jogs every evening after work.
Dad jogs every morning after work.
quests.hint: Two words need to change at the same time.
quests.explanation: Morning flips to evening, and before flips to after. The other choices change only one part.
quests.funFact: In hot weather, many people prefer to exercise in cooler times, like early morning or evening.

quests.instruction: In the bunk bed, Rafi sleeps on the upper bunk. His sister sleeps on the…
quests.hint: The bed you reach by ladder has a special name.
quests.explanation: The upper bunk is higher up. The lower bunk is the one below it.
quests.funFact: Bunk beds help families fit more beds into a small room.

quests.instruction: It started raining. Mira’s shoes were safe inside the cupboard, but her brother had left his…
quests.hint: Whose shoes are going to be soaked?
quests.explanation: Inside is within a shelter. Outside is in the open, where the rain falls.
quests.funFact: Rain falls when water droplets in clouds grow heavy enough to drop.

quests.instruction: The library opens at nine in the morning. Which word fits: “It ___ at six in the evening.”?
quests.hint: What does the librarian do after the last reader leaves?
quests.explanation: Opening lets people in. Closing finishes that, usually at the end of the day.
quests.funFact: The Library of Alexandria in ancient Egypt was one of the largest libraries of the ancient world.

quests.instruction: In the sentence “Mira’s grandparents arrive on Friday and depart on Monday,” which two words are opposites?
quests.hint: Look for the two actions: one is coming and the other is going.
quests.explanation: Arrive means to reach a place, and depart means to leave it. Friday and Monday are different days but not opposites.
quests.funFact: In English, Monday is named after the Moon.

quests.instruction: Which sentence contains a pair of opposite words?
quests.correctAnswer: Mum arrived early, but Dad got there late.
options: Mum arrived early, but Dad got there late.
Mum arrived early and Dad came soon after.
Mum arrived last and Dad was right behind her.
quests.hint: Which sentence puts two ideas at opposite ends?
quests.explanation: Early and late are opposites about time, and the sentence uses both. The other sentences describe order without an opposite pair.
quests.funFact: The proverb “better late than never” is hundreds of years old.
